232: /****************************************************************************
233:  * Name: bk7258_report_cache
234:  *
235:  * Description:
236:  *   Reports whether this core implements instruction and data caches, and is
237:  *   left in at boot so the next person does not have to guess.
238:  *
239:  *   The AP executes in place from flash at 0x02150000.  NuttX did not enable
240:  *   the instruction cache until commit "perf(bk7258): enable the AP
241:  *   instruction cache", and every instruction fetch was a flash access: the
242:  *   expression renderer cost ~455ms per frame for work that takes 0.09ms on a
243:  *   host, a 51200-byte word-at-a-time copy ran at 0.8MB/s, and raising the
244:  *   core to 480MHz changed none of it because the core was never the limit.
245:  *   The same frame now costs 37ms.
246:  *
247:  *   Turning it on needed two independent fixes, and the first one alone looks
248:  *   like "the cache does nothing": CONFIG_ARMV8M_ICACHE depends on the hidden
249:  *   ARMV8M_HAVE_ICACHE, which this chip's Kconfig did not select, so asking
250:  *   for it in a defconfig was silently dropped; and selecting it only compiles
251:  *   up_enable_icache() in -- every other ARMv8-M chip in the tree calls that
252:  *   from its own start code, this one did not.  Both are fixed now (see the
253:  *   chip Kconfig and bk7258_start.c).
254:  *
255:  *   Only the I-Cache is on.  Instruction fetch is read-only and needs no
256:  *   maintenance against the camera, panel and mailbox DMA that shares AP RAM,
257:  *   which the MPU deliberately keeps non-cacheable.
258:  *
259:  *   CLIDR/CTR exist in ARMv8-M whether or not a cache is fitted (they read
260:  *   zero when it is not), so reading them is safe and settles the question:
261:  *   this part reports CLIDR=0x09200003, i.e. both caches are implemented.
262:  *
263:  ****************************************************************************/
264: 
265: static void bk7258_report_cache(void)
266: {
267:   uint32_t clidr = getreg32(0xe000ed78);   /* SCB->CLIDR */
268:   uint32_t ctr   = getreg32(0xe000ed7c);   /* SCB->CTR   */
269:   unsigned int l1 = clidr & 7;
270: 
271:   printf("cache: CLIDR=0x%08" PRIx32 " CTR=0x%08" PRIx32
272:          " L1=%s%s%s\n", clidr, ctr,
273:          (l1 & 1) != 0 ? "I" : "",
274:          (l1 & 2) != 0 ? "D" : "",
275:          l1 == 0 ? "none (uncached XIP from flash)" :
276:          (l1 == 3 ? " (separate I and D)" : ""));
277: }

294:    * (BOARDIOC_FINALINIT) is never invoked in this minimal, apps-less NSH
295:    * configuration (no CONFIG_BOARDCTL_FINALINIT, no apps/nshlib start-up
296:    * script caller), so the test entry point is invoked here instead, from
297:    * the unconditionally-called CONFIG_BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE hook.  See
298:    * docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-gc9d01-lcd-bringup.md Task 3 Step 3.
299:    */
300: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_GC9D01_FB
301:   /* GC9D01 framebuffers, one per populated panel: fb_register() calls
302:    * up_fbinitialize(), which does the rail/reset/bus bring-up and the init
303:    * sequence and allocates a 51200-byte RGB565 framebuffer, then publishes
304:    * /dev/fb<display>.
305:    *
306:    * Both panels are registered unconditionally.  GC9D01 has no readable ID
307:    * register, so an unpopulated footprint cannot be distinguished from a
308:    * working panel -- every command still "completes".  Registering /dev/fb1
309:    * on a single-panel board therefore costs one unused 51200-byte buffer
310:    * and nothing else; refusing to register it would need board-variant
311:    * configuration that this board provides no way to detect.
312:    */
313: 
314:   {
315:     int display;
316:     int registered = 0;
317: 
318:     /* Both panels through reset and the command table in one pass, before
319:      * fb_register() asks for either of them.  The sequence is nearly all
320:      * waiting (20ms rail, 230ms reset pulse, 120ms after Sleep Out) and the
321:      * waits are the panels', not the bus's, so sharing them across the two
322:      * panels takes ~350ms off the time to the first pixel.  fb_register()
323:      * still calls up_fbinitialize() -> bk7258_gc9d01_panel_init(), which
324:      * finds its panel already up and returns.
325:      */
326: 
327:     (void)bk7258_gc9d01_panels_init((1 << GC9D01_NDISPLAYS) - 1);
328: 
329:     for (display = 0; display < GC9D01_NDISPLAYS; display++)
330:       {
331:         ret = fb_register(display, 0);
332:         if (ret < 0)
333:           {
334:             printf("fb_register(%d) failed: %d\n", display, ret);
335:             continue;
336:           }
337: 
338:         registered |= 1 << display;
339:         printf("fb: /dev/fb%d registered\n", display);
340:       }
341: 
342:     /* Boot greeting, written out rather than simply appearing.
343:      *
344:      * The panel has no readable ID register, so "the init sequence was sent"
345:      * has never been evidence that it worked; something has to be drawn at
346:      * boot or a dead panel looks exactly like a working one.
347:      *
348:      * Both panels are revealed together, one stroke segment per step, so the
349:      * word is written left to right.  The step count is the whole cost: the
350:      * panel takes no partial update, so every step pushes a full 51200-byte
351:      * frame to each panel at ~25ms, and the stroke rendering adds to that.
352:      * 20 steps measured 1677ms and was by itself most of the delay between
353:      * reset and a readable screen; 8 steps measured 408ms on the same board
354:      * and still reads as writing rather than appearing.  Keep it at 8 unless
355:      * there is a measurement to justify more.
356:      *
357:      * The pen-stroke version of this lives in the 'hello' shell command,
358:      * which has a proper stroke font.  It cannot be reused here: it is an
359:      * application, and this configuration builds neither exec_builtin() nor
360:      * posix_spawn(), so bring-up has no way to start it.
361:      */
362: 
363:     if (registered != 0)
364:       {
365:         (void)bk7258_gc9d01_fb_hello_animate(registered, 8);
366:       }
367:   }
368: #endif
369: 
370:   /* GC2145 camera: registered as a standard V4L2 /dev/video0 node here
371:    * (imgdata+imgsensor framework, see bk7258_camera_bringup.c), superseding
372:    * the older bare board_late_initialize() smoke-test call this line used
373:    * to make directly.  The old bk7258_gc2145_test() bare entry point is
374:    * kept as an independent NSH command (see bk7258_appinit.c) for
375:    * side-by-side diagnostic comparison, per design discussion in
376:    * docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-gc2145-camera-bringup.md -- it is
377:    * intentionally NOT called from here anymore, so a bug in this new V4L2
378:    * driver cannot be masked by (or confused with) the old direct-call
379:    * path still running unconditionally at boot. */
380:   (void)bk7258_camera_initialize();
381: 
382: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO
383:   /* Internal-DAC audio.  This has to come after bk7258_bringup() above,
384:    * not from inside it, for the same reason the camera does: the AUD block
385:    * needs the AUDP power domain and the AUD module clock, and both are

388:    * here must not take the console down with it.
389:    */
390: 
391:   (void)bk7258_audio_initialize();
392: #endif
393: 
394: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_JPEG_ENC
395:   /* After the camera: both want PSRAM, and registering the encoder second
396:    * keeps /dev/video0 belonging to capture and /dev/video1 to this codec no
397:    * matter how the framework numbers them internally.  Best-effort, like the
398:    * others -- a codec that fails to register must not take the console down.
399:    */
400: 
401:   (void)bk7258_jpeg_enc_initialize();

404: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_BLUETOOTH

406:    * bk7258_bt_bringup() above for why this is not part of bk7258_bringup().

2:  * app/camera_preview/camera_preview_main.c
3:  *
4:  * Live camera preview: GC2145 (640x480 packed 4:2:2, V Y1 U Y0 in memory)
5:  * -> GC9D01 (160x160 RGB565), pushed to every registered panel.
6:  *
7:  * Why this exists instead of `nxcamera; output /dev/fb0`: nxcamera's
8:  * show_image() passes the camera's own width and height as both source and
9:  * crop rectangle and gives libyuv only the framebuffer's stride, so it
10:  * would write a 640x480 image into a 160x160 framebuffer and run off the
11:  * end of it; and for a non-I420 source on an RGB565 panel it allocates
12:  * width*height*3/2 (460800 bytes) from the kernel heap, which on this board
13:  * holds roughly 300KB.  nxcamera also lives in the shared apps repository,
14:  * outside this project's scope, so it is left alone.
15:  *
16:  * Conversion: a single pass that samples the source directly into the
17:  * framebuffer, with no intermediate buffer at all.
18:  *
19:  *   centre-crop 480x480 out of 640x480, then take every 3rd pixel
20:  *   (480 / 160 == 3 exactly, so nearest-neighbour needs no arithmetic
21:  *   beyond an integer stride) and convert that chroma/luma group to RGB565.
22:  *
23:  * Going through libyuv would have meant staging I420 at crop size
24:  * (480*480*3/2 = 345600 bytes) and again at panel size, i.e. exactly the
25:  * allocation that defeats nxcamera on this board.  Sampling directly also
26:  * reads only ~100KB of the 614400-byte source frame per displayed frame,
27:  * which matters because PSRAM bandwidth is already the tightest resource
28:  * here (the capture path alone runs at ~37MB/s).
29:  *
30:  * The centre crop is what keeps the picture from being stretched: the panel
31:  * is a 160x160 round display, so a 4:3 frame is cropped to its central
32:  * square first.  The corners of that square are not visible on a round
33:  * panel -- that is a composition matter, not something this code hides.
34:  *
35:  * Dual panel: the board drives two GC9D01 screens (/dev/fb0 and /dev/fb1).
36:  * Conversion runs once into the first framebuffer and the result is copied
37:  * to the others, since both eyes show the same image.  The copy is 51200
38:  * bytes of kernel RAM, far cheaper than converting twice.  Each panel is
39:  * then pushed independently; at ~27ms per panel per frame the bus, not the
40:  * conversion, is the frame-rate limit.
41:  *
42:  * Usage:
43:  *   camera_preview [N] [options]        live preview, N frames (0 = forever)
44:  *   camera_preview live+face [N] [expr=<name>] [cycle=<sec>]
45:  *                                       fb0 live at the camera's full rate,
46:  *                                       fb1 an expression, repainted only
47:  *                                       when it changes
48:  *   camera_preview fill <hex> [options] static patterns, no camera involved
49:  *   camera_preview pattern|bars|grid [options]
50:  *   camera_preview face [name] [frames] [fps=N]
51:  *                                       draw an expression; no name lists them
52:  *
53:  * Options:
54:  *   fb=0 | fb=1 | fb=both   which panel(s) to drive (default both)
55:  *   jpeg | jpeg=N           also encode one frame in N through the hardware
56:  *                           JPEG encoder (/dev/video1); default N=60, about
57:  *                           two seconds at the measured rate
58:  *   jpegout=<path>          save the first encoded frame (needs a filesystem)
59:  *   jpegb64                 print every encoded frame as fenced base64, the
60:  *                           same form agent_camera uses, so
61:  *                           tools/b64frames.py rebuilds it without any
62:  *                           filesystem on the board
63:  *   q=N                     JPEG quality, default 80
64:  *   sat=N                   chroma gain in percent (default 100)
65:  *   gain=N                  luma gain in percent (default 100)
66:  *   full                    treat Y as full-range instead of 16..235
67:  *   uvswap                  exchange the Cb and Cr byte positions
68:  *   vyuy | uyvy | yuyv      YUV byte order (default vyuy, the hardware's)
69:  *   swap                    pre-byte-swap pattern pixels (see below)
70:  *
71:  * Why live+face and the encoder live in this one application: /dev/video0 has
72:  * a single owner, so while a preview streams nothing else can open the camera.

216: /* Colour pipeline tuning.
217:  *
218:  * The BT.601 limited-range coefficients below are correct as such
219:  * (298/409/100/208/516 == 1.164/1.596/0.391/0.813/2.018 in 8-bit fixed
220:  * point).
221:  *
222:  * On g_sat's value -- settled by measurement, after two wrong guesses.
223:  *
224:  * An earlier revision defaulted it to 150% claiming the chroma "barely leaves
225:  * neutral", citing the first 32 bytes of a frame.  That was 16 pixels from
226:  * the top-left corner, most likely a flat wall.  `camera_preview stats` now
227:  * measures whole frames, and a controlled pair settles it:
228:  *
229:  *   lens at a grey scene:        mean|U-128|=1  mean|V-128|=1  coloured=0%
230:  *   lens at a saturated object:  mean|U-128|=11 mean|V-128|=7  coloured=23%
231:  *
232:  * The chroma responds properly, so the sensor's colour path is fine and the
233:  * earlier "washed out" reading was just the scene.  White balance is neutral
234:  * too (U dev -1, V dev +1 on the grey scene), and exposure covers 11..254 of
235:  * the available range.  The GC2145 saturation registers are at their normal
236:  * defaults as well (page 2, 0xD1/0xD2 = 0x32; the 0xD1/0xD2 = 0x00 later in
237:  * the table is page 1 and unrelated).
238:  *
239:  * Conclusion: there is no colour defect to correct, so the default is 100 --
240:  * faithful reproduction.  g_sat and the per-channel gains stay as knobs for
241:  * subjective preference or for a future panel/sensor batch that does need
242:  * correcting, but nothing in the measurements justifies a non-unity default.
243:  *
244:  * These are run-time options rather than constants because colour is
245:  * subjective and needs iterating on the actual glass; baking a guess into
246:  * the firmware would cost a flash cycle per attempt.
247:  */
248: 
249: static int g_sat = 100;         /* chroma gain, percent (100 = faithful) */
250: static int g_gain = 100;        /* luma gain, percent */
251: static int g_gamma = 100;       /* tone curve exponent, percent (100 = off) */
252: static bool g_full_range;       /* Y spans 0..255 rather than 16..235 */
253: static bool g_uv_swap;          /* exchange U and V byte positions */
254: 
255: /* Cyclic shift applied when writing into the framebuffer.
256:  *
257:  * Diagnosing and correcting a horizontal offset between what the driver
258:  * thinks is column 0 and what the panel shows at its left edge.  The symptom
259:  * that motivated this is a vertical seam splitting the picture into two
260:  * halves: the row length is right (a wrong row length would shear the image
261:  * diagonally instead), but each row starts at the wrong column, so the two
262:  * parts swap sides and the wrap point shows up as a line.
263:  *
264:  * Shifting in the application is a *diagnostic*, not the final fix: once the
265:  * true offset is known it belongs in the panel driver's CASET/RASET window so
266:  * every framebuffer user benefits, not just this program.  Kept cyclic
267:  * (modulo the panel width) because that exactly inverts a wrap.
268:  */
269: 
270: static int g_xoff;
271: static int g_yoff;
272: 
273: /* Mirroring, for identifying the panel's scan direction.
274:  *
275:  * The ruler pattern showed green (drawn at y=0..3) appearing at the *bottom*
276:  * edge and blue (y=156..159) at the *top*, with red (x=156..159) on the left
277:  * -- i.e. both axes mirrored -- while the yellow centre line at x=80 stayed
278:  * centred, which rules out a cyclic shift (a shift of 80 would have moved
279:  * that line to the edge).
280:  *
281:  * The real fix for a mirrored panel is MADCTL (command 0x36) in the panel
282:  * driver's init table: bit7 MY = row order, bit6 MX = column order, so 0xC0
283:  * is a 180-degree rotation.  Doing it there costs nothing at run time and
284:  * fixes every /dev/fbN user.  These flags exist only to establish *which*
285:  * value is correct before committing it, since the vendor device table ships
286:  * 0x36 = 0x00 and whether that is right depends on how the module vendor
287:  * mounted the glass.
288:  */
289: 
290: static bool g_mirror_x;
291: static bool g_mirror_y;
292: 
293: /* Per-channel gain (white balance), percent.
294:  *
295:  * Motivation: the `bars` pattern showed the first six bars (black, blue,
296:  * green, cyan, red, magenta) reproduced correctly while yellow leaned green
297:  * and white leaned cyan.  Yellow is R+G and white is R+G+B, so both leaning
298:  * away from red while saturated red itself still looks red is the signature
299:  * of a red channel that is *low in gain* rather than missing.
300:  *
301:  * GC9D01 has no per-channel gain register -- its 0xF0/0xF1/0xF2/0xF3 entries
302:  * are a shared gamma curve -- so the correction belongs in the colour matrix.
303:  * Folding the gain into the coefficients rather than applying it afterwards
304:  * keeps it free of extra table lookups, which matter here: a lookup costs
305:  * ~1.4us on this platform (see preview_bench), so three per pixel would add
306:  * over 100ms to a frame.  The only added cost is two extra multiplies per
307:  * pixel for the luma term, and arithmetic is nearly free (25600 iterations
308:  * measured at 3ms).
309:  */
310: 
311: static int g_rgain = 100;
312: static int g_ggain = 100;
313: static int g_bgain = 100;
314: 
315: /* Tone curve, applied after the colour matrix.
316:  *
317:  * gamma=100 leaves it an identity table so the default path is bit-identical
318:  * to having no curve at all.  Below 100 lifts the mid-tones (makes a dark
319:  * picture brighter without clipping highlights), above 100 deepens them.
320:  * A table costs one SRAM read per channel; computing a power per pixel would
321:  * not fit the frame budget.
322:  *
323:  * Note the panel already applies its own gamma (the 0xF0/0xF1/0xF2/0xF3
324:  * entries in the GC9D01 init table), so this is a correction on top of that
325:  * rather than the primary gamma -- which is why the default is off.
326:  */
327: 
328: static uint8_t g_tone[256];
329: 
330: static void preview_build_tone(void)
331: {
332:   int i;
333: 
334:   for (i = 0; i < 256; i++)
335:     {
336:       if (g_gamma == 100)
337:         {
338:           g_tone[i] = (uint8_t)i;
339:         }
340:       else
341:         {
342:           /* out = 255 * (i/255)^(gamma/100), evaluated in double once per
343:            * run rather than per pixel.
344:            */
345: 
346:           double n = (double)i / 255.0;
347:           double e = (double)g_gamma / 100.0;
348:           int v = (int)(pow(n, e) * 255.0 + 0.5);
349: 
350:           g_tone[i] = (uint8_t)(v < 0 ? 0 : (v > 255 ? 255 : v));
351:         }
352:     }
353: }

369:  * before: CONFIG_TTY_SIGINT (which was set) delivers SIGINT to the pid NSH
370:  * registers with TIOCSCTTY, and CONFIG_SIG_DEFAULT (which was NOT set)
371:  * supplies the default action.  Without the latter a process that installs
372:  * no handler simply ignores the signal, which is why an earlier Ctrl-C probe
373:  * (app/ctrlc_test) appeared to work -- it installs a handler --
374:  * while this loop did not.  Installing a handler here means the exit no
375:  * longer depends on that config at all.
376:  */

387: /****************************************************************************
388:  * Name: preview_claim_ctty
389:  *
390:  * Description:
391:  *   Registers this task as the console's controlling terminal, so that a
392:  *   0x03 on the wire turns into a SIGINT delivered here.
393:  *
394:  *   This is not something an application would normally have to do -- NSH is
395:  *   supposed to do it for the foreground task (nsh_builtin.c calls
396:  *   TIOCSCTTY with the child pid before waitpid).  On this board it does not
397:  *   happen: measured with app/ctrlc_test's probe, TIOCSCTTY from inside a
398:  *   freshly started builtin returns 0, i.e. the terminal was still
399:  *   *unclaimed*.  uart_check_special() requires dev->pid > 0, so without
400:  *   this call no amount of Ctrl-C produces a signal, which is exactly why
401:  *   the preview could not be stopped.  Why NSH skips it is still open; the
402:  *   probe reports it in one line and is worth re-running after any NSH or
403:  *   serial change.
404:  *
405:  *   Claiming it also has to be undone (preview_release_ctty), because
406:  *   drivers/serial/serial.c refuses to move an already-set owner: a second
407:  *   TIOCSCTTY returns -EINVAL.  Leaving it set would point SIGINT at a dead
408:  *   pid and break the *next* run.
409:  *
410:  ****************************************************************************/
411: 
412: static void preview_claim_ctty(void)
413: {
414:   if (ioctl(STDIN_FILENO, TIOCSCTTY, (unsigned long)getpid()) == 0)
415:     {
416:       g_ctty_claimed = true;
417:     }
418:   else if (errno != EINVAL)
419:     {
420:       printf("preview: TIOCSCTTY failed: %d (Ctrl-C may not work)\n", errno);
421:     }
422: }
423: 
424: static void preview_release_ctty(void)
425: {
426:   if (g_ctty_claimed)
427:     {
428:       ioctl(STDIN_FILENO, TIOCNOTTY, 0);
429:       g_ctty_claimed = false;
430:     }
431: }

433: /****************************************************************************
434:  * Name: preview_print_b64
435:  *
436:  * Description:
437:  *   Emit an encoded frame on the console in the same fenced base64 form
438:  *   agent_camera uses, so tools/b64frames.py rebuilds either one and the two
439:  *   paths can be compared byte for byte.  It exists here because the two
440:  *   paths do not agree: the hardware JPEG path (agent_camera, /dev/video0 in
441:  *   JPEG mode) mis-assembles its bitstream -- consecutive frames of a static
442:  *   scene came back differing by 50 to 140 grey levels, the tail of each
443:  *   picture belonging to a different frame, while every marker check passed
444:  *   -- whereas this path encodes a frame that came through the verified UYVY
445:  *   capture, so it is the one to trust for evidence.
446:  *
447:  ****************************************************************************/
448: 
449: static void preview_print_b64(FAR const uint8_t *data, size_t len)
450: {
451:   static const char tbl[] =
452:     "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
453:   uint32_t hash = 2166136261u;
454:   size_t i;
455: 
456:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
457:     {
458:       hash ^= data[i];
459:       hash *= 16777619u;
460:     }
461: 
462:   printf("agent_camera: payload len=%zu fnv1a=0x%08" PRIx32 "\n", len, hash);
463:   printf("-----BEGIN AGENT_CAMERA JPEG %zu-----\n", len);
464: 
465:   for (i = 0; i < len; i += 3)
466:     {
467:       size_t remain = len - i;
468:       uint32_t v = (uint32_t)data[i] << 16;
469:       char quad[4];
470: 
471:       if (remain > 1)
472:         {
473:           v |= (uint32_t)data[i + 1] << 8;
474:         }
475: 
476:       if (remain > 2)
477:         {
478:           v |= data[i + 2];
479:         }
480: 
481:       quad[0] = tbl[(v >> 18) & 0x3f];
482:       quad[1] = tbl[(v >> 12) & 0x3f];
483:       quad[2] = remain > 1 ? tbl[(v >> 6) & 0x3f] : '=';
484:       quad[3] = remain > 2 ? tbl[v & 0x3f] : '=';
485: 
486:       fwrite(quad, 1, 4, stdout);
487: 
488:       if ((i / 3) % 19 == 18)
489:         {
490:           putchar('\n');
491: 
492:           /* Same throttle as agent_camera_print_b64(), and for the same
493:            * reason: the AP's console is a mailbox bridge holding 1024 bytes,
494:            * and an unthrottled 33KB burst arrives truncated -- measured
495:            * 2026-08-17, a 12-frame dump came back with 2 of 12 fences intact
496:            * and both bodies short.  Pausing every two lines keeps the writer
497:            * under the bridge's drain rate.
498:            */
499: 
500:           if (((i / 3) / 19) % 2 == 1)
501:             {
502:               fflush(stdout);
503:               usleep(30000);
504:             }
505:         }
506:     }
507: 
508:   putchar('\n');
509:   printf("-----END AGENT_CAMERA JPEG-----\n");
510: }
511:

515: 
516:   clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
517:   return (uint32_t)(ts.tv_sec * 1000 + ts.tv_nsec / 1000000);
518: }

607: static int preview_open_camera(FAR struct preview_s *p)
608: {
609:   struct v4l2_requestbuffers req;
610:   struct v4l2_buffer buf;
611:   struct v4l2_format fmt;
612:   int i;
613: 
614:   p->camfd = open(CAM_DEV, O_RDWR);
615:   if (p->camfd < 0)
616:     {
617:       printf("preview: open %s failed: %d\n", CAM_DEV, errno);
618:       return -errno;
619:     }
620: 
621:   memset(&fmt, 0, sizeof(fmt));
622:   fmt.type                = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
623:   fmt.fmt.pix.width       = CAM_WIDTH;
624:   fmt.fmt.pix.height      = CAM_HEIGHT;
625:   fmt.fmt.pix.field       = V4L2_FIELD_ANY;
626: 
627:   /* The real memory layout is V Y1 U Y0 (see preview_convert()), which no
628:    * V4L2 fourcc names: VYUY gets the chroma right but not the reversed luma
629:    * pair, and the imgsensor/imgdata layers this driver sits on define only
630:    * UYVY and YUYV anyway.  UYVY is therefore what both sides agree to call
631:    * it -- a label for "packed 4:2:2, chroma first", with the exact order
632:    * documented in the driver and decoded by preview_convert().  Agreeing
633:    * with the driver is necessary (VIDIOC_S_FMT fails otherwise) but not
634:    * sufficient: both sides can be wrong in the same direction without any
635:    * layer complaining, which is how the chroma swap survived this long.
636:    */
637: 
638:   fmt.fmt.pix.pixelformat = V4L2_PIX_FMT_UYVY;
639: 
640:   if (ioctl(p->camfd, VIDIOC_S_FMT, (uintptr_t)&fmt) < 0)
641:     {
642:       printf("preview: VIDIOC_S_FMT failed: %d\n", errno);
643:       return -errno;
644:     }
645: 
646:   memset(&req, 0, sizeof(req));
647:   req.type   = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
648:   req.memory = V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP;
649:   req.count  = NBUFFERS;
650: 
651:   if (ioctl(p->camfd, VIDIOC_REQBUFS, (uintptr_t)&req) < 0)
652:     {
653:       printf("preview: VIDIOC_REQBUFS failed: %d\n", errno);
654:       return -errno;
655:     }
656: 
657:   p->nbuffers = req.count < NBUFFERS ? req.count : NBUFFERS;
658: 
659:   for (i = 0; i < p->nbuffers; i++)
660:     {
661:       memset(&buf, 0, sizeof(buf));
662:       buf.type   = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
663:       buf.memory = V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP;
664:       buf.index  = i;
665: 
666:       if (ioctl(p->camfd, VIDIOC_QUERYBUF, (uintptr_t)&buf) < 0)
667:         {
668:           printf("preview: VIDIOC_QUERYBUF(%d) failed: %d\n", i, errno);
669:           return -errno;
670:         }
671: 
672:       p->bufs[i] = mmap(NULL, buf.length, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
673:                         MAP_SHARED, p->camfd, buf.m.offset);
674:       if (p->bufs[i] == MAP_FAILED)
675:         {
676:           printf("preview: buffer %d mmap failed: %d\n", i, errno);

697: /****************************************************************************
698:  * Name: preview_draw_pattern
699:  *
700:  * Description:
701:  *   Static self-test patterns, drawn straight into the framebuffer and
702:  *   pushed once.  These exist to split "the panel shows nothing
703:  *   recognisable" into independent questions without a re-flash per
704:  *   hypothesis:
705:  *
706:  *     fill <hex>  uniform colour.  If this is uniform on the glass, the
707:  *                 transport is sound and any remaining fault is format or
708:  *                 geometry.  If it is uniform but the WRONG colour, it is
709:  *                 byte order.  If it is noise, the transport itself drops
710:  *                 or reorders bytes.
711:  *     pattern     four quadrants + black border.  Colour error, stride
712:  *                 error and window error each look different here, so one
713:  *                 look tells you which of the three it is.
714:  *     bars        8 vertical colour bars.  A single dropped byte shears
715:  *                 every bar below the drop, which a uniform fill hides.
716:  *     grid        1-pixel checkerboard, the worst case for the bus: any
717:  *                 dropped or duplicated word turns the regular lattice
718:  *                 into visible diagonal banding.
719:  *
720:  *   Appending "swap" writes each pixel pre-byte-swapped, which cancels the
721:  *   driver's own swap.  That makes the wire byte order testable from user
722:  *   space: exactly one of `fill f800` and `fill f800 swap` shows red.
723:  *
724:  ****************************************************************************/
725: 
726: static uint16_t preview_pat_bar(int i)
727: {
728:   static const uint16_t bars[8] =
729:   {
730:     0x0000, 0x001f, 0x07e0, 0x07ff, 0xf800, 0xf81f, 0xffe0, 0xffff
731:   };
732: 
733:   return bars[i & 7];
734: }
735: 
736: static int preview_draw_pattern(FAR struct preview_s *p, int argc,
737:                                 FAR char *argv[])
738: {
739:   FAR const char *what = argv[1];
740:   int dw = p->vinfo.xres;
741:   int dh = p->vinfo.yres;
742:   bool swap = false;
743:   uint16_t colour = 0xf800;
744:   int ox = ((g_xoff % dw) + dw) % dw;
745:   int oy = ((g_yoff % dh) + dh) % dh;
746: 
747:   int x;
748:   int y;
749:   int i;
750: 
751:   for (i = 2; i < argc; i++)
752:     {
753:       if (strcmp(argv[i], "swap") == 0)
754:         {
755:           swap = true;
756:         }
757:       else if (strncmp(argv[i], "fb=", 3) != 0 &&
758:                strncmp(argv[i], "sat=", 4) != 0 &&
759:                strncmp(argv[i], "gain=", 5) != 0 &&
760:                strncmp(argv[i], "gamma=", 6) != 0 &&
761:                strncmp(argv[i], "xoff=", 5) != 0 &&
762:                strncmp(argv[i], "yoff=", 5) != 0 &&
763:                strcmp(argv[i], "mx") != 0 &&
764:                strcmp(argv[i], "my") != 0 &&
765:                strcmp(argv[i], "rot180") != 0 &&
766:                strncmp(argv[i], "rgain=", 6) != 0 &&
767:                strncmp(argv[i], "ggain=", 6) != 0 &&
768:                strncmp(argv[i], "bgain=", 6) != 0)
769:         {
770:           colour = (uint16_t)strtoul(argv[i], NULL, 16);
771:         }
772:     }
773: 
774:   for (y = 0; y < dh; y++)
775:     {
776:       int ty = y + oy;
777:       FAR uint16_t *drow;
778: 
779:       if (ty >= dh)
780:         {
781:           ty -= dh;
782:         }
783: 
784:       if (g_mirror_y)
785:         {
786:           ty = dh - 1 - ty;
787:         }
788: 
789:       drow = (FAR uint16_t *)(p->fbmem[0] + (size_t)ty * p->pinfo.stride);
790: 
791:       for (x = 0; x < dw; x++)
792:         {
793:           int tx = x + ox;
794:           uint16_t c;
795: 
796:           if (tx >= dw)
797:             {
798:               tx -= dw;
799:             }
800: 
801:           if (g_mirror_x)
802:             {
803:               tx = dw - 1 - tx;
804:             }
805: 
806:           if (strcmp(what, "fill") == 0)
807:             {
808:               c = colour;
809:             }
810:           else if (strcmp(what, "bars") == 0)
811:             {
812:               c = preview_pat_bar(x * 8 / dw);
813:             }
814:           else if (strcmp(what, "grid") == 0)
815:             {
816:               c = ((x ^ y) & 1) ? 0xffff : 0x0000;
817:             }
818:           else if (strcmp(what, "ruler") == 0)
819:             {
820:               /* Edge markers that make a shift readable by eye.  Each edge
821:                * gets its own colour, so wherever the white band appears is
822:                * where the driver's column 0 actually lands on the glass, and
823:                * the yellow centre line says whether the shift is half a
824:                * screen (the "seam down the middle" case) or something else.
825:                *
826:                *   white  x = 0..3      left edge
827:                *   red    x = 156..159  right edge
828:                *   green  y = 0..3      top edge
829:                *   blue   y = 156..159  bottom edge
830:                *   yellow x = 80        centre
831:                */
832: 
833:               if (x < 4)
834:                 {
835:                   c = 0xffff;                    /* white  */
836:                 }
837:               else if (x >= dw - 4)
838:                 {
839:                   c = 0xf800;                    /* red    */
840:                 }
841:               else if (y < 4)
842:                 {
843:                   c = 0x07e0;                    /* green  */
844:                 }
845:               else if (y >= dh - 4)
846:                 {
847:                   c = 0x001f;                    /* blue   */
848:                 }
849:               else if (x == dw / 2)
850:                 {
851:                   c = 0xffe0;                    /* yellow */
852:                 }
853:               else
854:                 {
855:                   c = 0x0000;
856:                 }
857:             }
858:           else if (strcmp(what, "wb") == 0)
859:             {
860:               /* White-balance ladder: five horizontal bands, each showing
861:                * white (left half) and yellow (right half) with G and B
862:                * progressively attenuated.  Pick the band that looks most
863:                * neutral / most yellow and use its percentage as ggain and
864:                * bgain for the live path.
865:                *
866:                * Attenuating G and B rather than boosting R is deliberate:
867:                * white is 0xFFFF, so R is already at its maximum 31 and
868:                * cannot be raised.  A multiplicative correction can only
869:                * bring the other channels down.
870:                *
871:                * Bands top to bottom: 100%, 92%, 84%, 76%, 68%.
872:                */
873: 
874:               static const int gb[5] =
875:               {
876:                 100, 92, 84, 76, 68
877:               };
878: 
879:               int band = y * 5 / dh;
880:               int k = gb[band > 4 ? 4 : band];
881:               int rr = 31;
882:               int gg = 63 * k / 100;
883:               int bb = (x < dw / 2) ? (31 * k / 100) : 0;
884: 
885:               c = (uint16_t)((rr << 11) | (gg << 5) | bb);
886:             }
887:           else /* "pattern" */
888:             {
889:               if (x < 4 || y < 4 || x >= dw - 4 || y >= dh - 4)
890:                 {
891:                   c = 0x0000;
892:                 }
893:               else if (y < dh / 2)
894:                 {
895:                   c = (x < dw / 2) ? 0xf800 : 0x07e0;
896:                 }
897:               else
898:                 {
899:                   c = (x < dw / 2) ? 0x001f : 0xffff;
900:                 }
901:             }
902: 
903:           drow[tx] = swap ? (uint16_t)((c >> 8) | (c << 8)) : c;
904:         }
905:     }
906: 
907:   for (i = 1; i < p->nfb; i++)
908:     {
909:       memcpy(p->fbmem[i], p->fbmem[0], p->pinfo.fblen);
910:     }
911: 
912:   printf("preview: drew '%s'%s on %dx%d, %d panel(s), xoff=%d yoff=%d "
913:          "mirror=%s%s\n", what, swap ? " (pre-swapped)" : "", dw, dh,
914:          p->nfb, ox, oy, g_mirror_x ? "X" : "-", g_mirror_y ? "Y" : "-");
915: 
916:   return OK;
917: }

919: /****************************************************************************
920:  * Name: preview_convert
921:  *
922:  * Description:
923:  *   One frame: centre-crop, 3:1 nearest-neighbour downscale and packed
924:  *   4:2:2 YUV to RGB565, straight from the capture buffer into the first
925:  *   framebuffer.  BT.601 coefficients in 8-bit fixed point; the shifts are
926:  *   chosen so the whole conversion stays in 32-bit integer math.
927:  *
928:  *   Byte order is V Y1 U Y0: each 4-byte group carries two pixels, with the
929:  *   chroma pair shared between them, but *reversed* -- byte 0 is Cr, byte 2
930:  *   is Cb, and byte 3 is the luma of the left (even) column while byte 1 is
931:  *   the luma of the right (odd) one.  A source x therefore maps to group
932:  *   (x >> 1) and picks byte 3 or byte 1 by x's parity.
933:  *
934:  *   How that was settled.  Three claims have to be separated, and each has
935:  *   its own evidence:
936:  *
937:  *   (1) Which bytes are luma.  Bytes 1 and 3.  Decoding with luma at bytes
938:  *       0/2 was photographed on the panel and gave a geometrically correct,
939:  *       clearly recognisable picture in which every pixel was either
940:  *       saturated green or magenta.  That is the arithmetic signature of
941:  *       feeding chroma into the luma term: with y_code == (U-16)*298 ≈ 33376
942:  *       constant and u_code == v_code == Y-128 == t,
943:  *
944:  *           r = (33376 + 409t) >> 8 = 130 + 1.6t
945:  *           g = (33376 - 308t) >> 8 = 130 - 1.2t
946:  *           b = (33376 + 516t) >> 8 = 130 + 2.0t
947:  *
948:  *       so t < 0 (dark) drives green and t > 0 (bright) drives magenta while
949:  *       luma structure survives, because t still carries it.  A captured
950:  *       frame agrees: over /tmp/frame.yuv, bytes 1 and 3 have sd 39 and span
951:  *       18..153, bytes 0 and 2 have sd 6.2 and 2.3 around 128.
952:  *
953:  *   (2) In which order the two luma samples sit.  Reversed: byte 3 is the
954:  *       left pixel.  Natural images are equally smooth across every pixel
955:  *       boundary, so mean |dY| between the two samples *inside* a group must
956:  *       match mean |dY| *across* the group boundary.  On the captured frame
957:  *       it does not: 1.752 inside versus 3.787 across, a factor of 2.16.
958:  *       Un-swapping the two luma bytes makes it 1.752 versus 1.760 -- and
959:  *       1.76 is also what the same measurement gives vertically (1.621),
960:  *       where no byte ordering is involved.  The asymmetry is the fingerprint
961:  *       of a pair read out backwards: the "across" difference then spans
962:  *       three columns instead of one.
963:  *
964:  *   (3) Which chroma byte is Cb.  Byte 2.  This follows from (2) once the
965:  *       sensor's bus order is known.  The GC2145 is configured with register
966:  *       0x84 = 0x02 (dvp_gc2145.c, commented "yuyv"), which the part's
967:  *       output-format table defines as Y Cb Y Cr on the wire -- corroborated
968:  *       by Zephyr's driver, where VIDEO_PIX_FMT_YUYV maps to
969:  *       GC2145_REG_OUTPUT_FMT_YCBYCR = 0x02.  A group in memory whose luma
970:  *       samples are reversed *and* whose chroma sits at bytes 0/2 is exactly
971:  *       the four bus bytes stored backwards: Y0 Cb Y1 Cr -> Cr Y1 Cb Y0.
972:  *       So byte 0 is Cr and byte 2 is Cb.  Scene evidence agrees: on
973:  *       frame.yuv (red text on a white sign) the extreme chroma deviations
974:  *       are byte0 +57 and byte2 -18, a ratio of -3.17, against -2.96
975:  *       predicted for pure red read as (Cr, Cb) -- and a poor match for blue
976:  *       read the other way round (-6.2 predicted).
977:  *
978:  *   What this fixed.  The decode used to assume plain UYVY (Cb at byte 0),
979:  *   which swaps Cb and Cr and so rotates every hue about the red/blue axis:
980:  *   structure, brightness and grey balance all stay right, which is why the
981:  *   symptom was only "colours a bit off" rather than an obviously broken
982:  *   image.  Reds came out blue.  The luma pair order was wrong at the same
983:  *   time, but that only misplaces detail by one source column and is
984:  *   invisible after the 3:1 downscale.
985:  *
986:  *   Note the layout is not any V4L2 fourcc: VYUY would describe the chroma
987:  *   correctly but not the reversed luma pair.  The driver still advertises
988:  *   V4L2_PIX_FMT_UYVY because that is the closest order the imgsensor and
989:  *   imgdata layers define; see bk7258_camera_imgsensor.c.
990:  *
991:  *   Saturation: with the chroma decoded correctly `camera_preview stats`
992:  *   measures a normal chroma swing (mean |U-128| = 11 on a saturated scene,
993:  *   1 on a grey one), so no correction is applied by default.  g_sat,
994:  *   g_gain, g_full_range and g_uv_swap remain as knobs because colour is
995:  *   subjective and needs the real panel in the loop.
996:  *
997:  ****************************************************************************/
998: 
999: /* One source row's worth of the cropped region, staged in SRAM.
1000:  *
1001:  * Why this exists: the capture buffer is in PSRAM, mapped non-cacheable, and
1002:  * a single CPU read of it costs on the order of microseconds.  Measured:
1003:  * converting one 160x160 frame with per-pixel reads straight out of PSRAM
1004:  * took 194ms, i.e. ~7.6us per output pixel -- about 2400 CPU cycles at
1005:  * 320MHz for what is a load plus a dozen arithmetic instructions.  Reducing
1006:  * the number of reads per pixel from three to one changed nothing (180ms ->
1007:  * 194ms, inside the noise), which is what ruled out access *count* and
1008:  * pointed at per-access *latency*.
1009:  *
1010:  * A bulk memcpy, by contrast, is sequential and lets the PSRAM controller
1011:  * burst.  So each needed row is copied once and then read repeatedly out of
1012:  * SRAM.
1013:  *
1014:  * Only the cropped span is staged: the centre 480 of 640 columns is quad
1015:  * indices CROP_X/2 .. (CROP_X+CROP_SIZE)/2, i.e. 240 quads = 960 bytes,
1016:  * instead of the full 1280-byte row.  Static rather than on the stack
1017:  * because this app's STACKSIZE is 4096.
1018:  */
1019: 
1020: #define ROW_QUADS   (CROP_SIZE / 2)            /* 240 */
1021: #define ROW_BYTES   (ROW_QUADS * 4)            /* 960 */
1022: #define ROW_Q0      (CROP_X / 2)               /* first quad index staged */
1023: 
1024: static uint32_t g_rowbuf[ROW_QUADS];
1025: 
1026: /****************************************************************************
1027:  * Name: preview_bench
1028:  *
1029:  * Description:
1030:  *   Micro-benchmarks of the accesses the conversion loop actually makes.
1031:  *
1032:  *   This exists because two rounds of "obvious" optimisation both failed:
1033:  *   collapsing three per-pixel PSRAM byte reads into one 32-bit read changed
1034:  *   convert time from 180ms to 194ms (nothing), and staging each row in SRAM
1035:  *   with memcpy made it 456ms (worse).  Both were reasoning from a guess
1036:  *   about where the time went.  The numbers below separate the candidates so
1037:  *   the next change can be aimed rather than tried.
1038:  *
1039:  *   What each line isolates:
1040:  *     arith      the arithmetic alone, no frame memory touched at all
1041:  *     sram rnd   same access pattern as the real loop, but out of SRAM
1042:  *     psram seq  consecutive 32-bit reads from the capture buffer
1043:  *     psram rnd  the real loop's stride (one quad per 1.5 quads)
1044:  *     memcpy     bulk sequential PSRAM -> SRAM, the failed optimisation
1045:  *
1046:  *   Interpretation: if `psram rnd` dominates and `sram rnd` is small, the
1047:  *   cost is per-access PSRAM latency, and the fix has to reduce accesses or
1048:  *   make them cacheable -- not reorder them.
1049:  *
1050:  ****************************************************************************/
1051: 
1052: #define BENCH_N  25600      /* one frame's worth of output pixels */
1053: 
1054: static void preview_bench(FAR struct preview_s *p)
1055: {
1056:   FAR const volatile uint32_t *ps;
1057:   uint32_t t;
1058:   uint32_t acc = 0;
1059:   int i;
1060: 
1061:   if (p->camfd < 0 || p->bufs[0] == NULL)
1062:     {
1063:       printf("bench: no capture buffer\n");
1064:       return;
1065:     }
1066: 
1067:   ps = (FAR const volatile uint32_t *)p->bufs[0];
1068: 
1069:   t = now_ms();
1070:   for (i = 0; i < BENCH_N; i++)
1071:     {
1072:       acc += (uint32_t)(i * 409 + 128) >> 8;
1073:     }
1074: 
1075:   printf("bench: arith     %u iters in %ums\n", BENCH_N,
1076:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));
1077: 
1078:   t = now_ms();
1079:   for (i = 0; i < BENCH_N; i++)
1080:     {
1081:       acc += g_rowbuf[i % ROW_QUADS];
1082:     }
1083: 
1084:   printf("bench: sram rnd  %u reads in %ums\n", BENCH_N,
1085:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));
1086: 
1087:   t = now_ms();
1088:   for (i = 0; i < BENCH_N; i++)
1089:     {
1090:       acc += ps[i];
1091:     }
1092: 
1093:   printf("bench: psram seq %u reads in %ums\n", BENCH_N,
1094:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));
1095: 
1096:   t = now_ms();
1097:   for (i = 0; i < BENCH_N; i++)
1098:     {
1099:       /* Same stride the converter uses: 3 source pixels per output pixel,
1100:        * two source pixels per quad.
1101:        */
1102: 
1103:       acc += ps[(i * 3) >> 1];
1104:     }
1105: 
1106:   printf("bench: psram rnd %u reads in %ums\n", BENCH_N,
1107:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));
1108: 
1109:   t = now_ms();
1110:   for (i = 0; i < 160; i++)
1111:     {
1112:       memcpy(g_rowbuf, (FAR const void *)(p->bufs[0] + i * CAM_WIDTH * 2),
1113:              ROW_BYTES);
1114:     }
1115: 
1116:   printf("bench: memcpy    160 x %u bytes in %ums\n", ROW_BYTES,
1117:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));
1118: 
1119:   /* The converter's exact address sequence: 160 sampled rows, each 3 source
1120:    * rows apart, 160 quads per row.  The plain "psram rnd" case above stays
1121:    * inside the first 153600 bytes, while this one walks all 614400 -- if
1122:    * PSRAM has row/page miss penalties, only this case will show them, and
1123:    * that is the difference that the flat 14ms of read+arith+write fails to
1124:    * explain against a measured 194ms convert.
1125:    */
1126: 
1127:   t = now_ms();
1128:   for (i = 0; i < 160; i++)
1129:     {
1130:       FAR const volatile uint32_t *row =
1131:         (FAR const volatile uint32_t *)(p->bufs[0] +
1132:                                         (size_t)(i * 3) * CAM_WIDTH * 2);
1133:       int k;
1134: 
1135:       for (k = 0; k < 160; k++)
1136:         {
1137:           acc += row[(CROP_X + k * 3) >> 1];
1138:         }
1139:     }
1140: 
1141:   printf("bench: psram rows 160x160 strided reads in %ums\n",
1142:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t));
1143: 
1144:   /* Framebuffer is kernel SRAM; included to confirm the write side is not a
1145:    * factor.
1146:    */
1147: 
1148:   t = now_ms();
1149:   for (i = 0; i < BENCH_N; i++)
1150:     {
1151:       ((FAR uint16_t *)p->fbmem[0])[i % (GC9D01_PIXELS)] = (uint16_t)i;
1152:     }
1153: 
1154:   printf("bench: fb write  %u writes in %ums (acc=%u)\n", BENCH_N,
1155:          (unsigned int)(now_ms() - t), (unsigned int)acc);
1156: }

1158: /****************************************************************************
1159:  * Name: preview_stats
1160:  *
1161:  * Description:
1162:  *   Objective statistics of one captured frame.
1163:  *
1164:  *   Why this exists: judging the *panel* needs a human eye or a colorimeter,
1165:  *   but judging the *source* does not.  Colour flows camera -> YUV -> RGB ->
1166:  *   panel, and everything except the last hop is measurable from software.
1167:  *   Earlier rounds asked for photographs to diagnose things that were
1168:  *   actually decidable here.
1169:  *
1170:  *   How to read the output:
1171:  *
1172:  *     U/V mean    A neutral grey or white subject should give both near 128.
1173:  *                 A consistent offset is the camera's white balance, and the
1174:  *                 offset directly yields the per-channel gain needed:
1175:  *                 V > 128 means the source leans red, U > 128 leans blue.
1176:  *     Y min/max   The usable dynamic range.  A washed-out ("greyish")
1177:  *                 picture with correct decoding usually means Y occupies far
1178:  *                 less than 16..235, which no amount of chroma gain fixes --
1179:  *                 that needs exposure or a contrast stretch.
1180:  *     Y histogram Where the tones actually sit; a single tall bucket means a
1181:  *                 flat, low-contrast frame.
1182:  *
1183:  *   Sampling every 4th quad keeps this to ~77k PSRAM reads (~18ms at the
1184:  *   measured 0.23us each) while still covering the whole frame.
1185:  *
1186:  ****************************************************************************/
1187: 
1188: static void preview_stats(FAR struct preview_s *p, int index)
1189: {
1190:   FAR const uint32_t *q = (FAR const uint32_t *)p->bufs[index];
1191:   FAR const struct preview_order_s *ord = &g_orders[g_yuv_order];
1192:   uint32_t nquads = (CAM_WIDTH * CAM_HEIGHT) / 2;
1193:   uint32_t hist[16];
1194:   uint32_t ysum = 0;
1195:   uint32_t usum = 0;
1196:   uint32_t vsum = 0;
1197:   uint32_t uabs = 0;      /* sum |U-128|, quantifies saturation */
1198:   uint32_t vabs = 0;
1199:   uint32_t csat = 0;      /* samples with |U-128|>16 or |V-128|>16 */
1200:   int ymin = 255;
1201:   int ymax = 0;
1202:   int umin = 255;
1203:   int umax = 0;
1204:   int vmin = 255;
1205:   int vmax = 0;
1206:   uint32_t n = 0;

440: /****************************************************************************
441:  * Name: sc_conflicting
442:  *
443:  * Description:
444:  *   Two cues that both read strongly and point in different directions.  The
445:  *   skill document forces "unable to judge" here; without this check the
446:  *   policy would happily report whichever cue the model listed first, which
447:  *   is the failure mode the rule exists to prevent.
448:  *
449:  ****************************************************************************/
450: 
451: static bool sc_conflicting(const struct sc_verdict_s *v)
452: {
453:   int strong = 0;
454:   int i;
455: 
456:   for (i = 0; i < v->ncues; i++)
457:     {
458:       if (v->cues[i].confidence >= SC_CONFLICT_CONF)
459:         {
460:           strong++;
461:         }
462:     }
463: 
464:   return strong >= 2;

467: /****************************************************************************
468:  * Name: sc_notify
469:  *
470:  * Description:
471:  *   Apply the confidence policy and produce the wearer-facing line.  This is
472:  *   the whole product logic in one place, on purpose.
473:  *
474:  ****************************************************************************/
475: 
476: static void sc_notify(const struct sc_verdict_s *v)
477: {
478:   if (v->unable)
479:     {
480:       printf("social_cue: SAY  \"看不清表情，判断不了（%s）。\"\n", v->reason);
481:       printf("social_cue: policy unable_to_judge=true reason=%s\n", v->reason);
482:       sc_buzz(1, 400, 0);
483:       return;
484:     }
485: 
486:   if (sc_conflicting(v))
487:     {
488:       printf("social_cue: SAY  \"信号不一致，%s 和 %s 都很明显，直接问一句更稳。\"\n",
489:              v->cues[0].meaning, v->cues[1].meaning);
490:       printf("social_cue: policy conflicting_cues -> withheld a verdict\n");
491:       sc_buzz(1, 400, 0);
492:       return;
493:     }
494: 
495:   if (v->overall < SC_CONF_WEAK)
496:     {
497:       printf("social_cue: SAY  \"没有明显线索，判断不了。\"\n");
498:       printf("social_cue: policy overall=%.2f < %.2f -> unable\n",
499:              (double)v->overall, (double)SC_CONF_WEAK);
500:       sc_buzz(1, 400, 0);
501:       return;
502:     }
503: 
504:   if (v->overall < SC_CONF_REPORT)
505:     {
506:       printf("social_cue: SAY  \"可能有点%s，不过这个判断不太确定。\"\n",
507:              v->cues[0].meaning);
508:       printf("social_cue: policy overall=%.2f in [%.2f,%.2f) -> cue only, "
509:              "no suggestion\n", (double)v->overall,
510:              (double)SC_CONF_WEAK, (double)SC_CONF_REPORT);
511:       sc_buzz(2, 80, 120);
512:       return;
513:     }
514: 
515:   printf("social_cue: SAY  \"他%s（%s，%.0f%%）。建议：%s。\"\n",
516:          v->cues[0].cue, v->cues[0].meaning,
517:          (double)(v->overall * 100.0f), v->suggestion);
518:   printf("social_cue: policy overall=%.2f >= %.2f -> cue + suggestion\n",
519:          (double)v->overall, (double)SC_CONF_REPORT);
520:   sc_buzz(2, 80, 120);

573:  * Name: sc_cycle
574:  ****************************************************************************/

576: static int sc_cycle(bool real_capture, const struct sc_verdict_s *verdict)
577: {
578:   enum sc_state_e state = SC_IDLE;
579:   ssize_t frame_len = 0;
580: 
581:   g_cancelled = 0;
582: 
583:   sc_enter(&state, SC_CAPTURING);
584:   sc_buzz(1, 60, 0);

586:   if (real_capture)
587:     {
588:       frame_len = sc_capture();

590:         {
591:           printf("social_cue: capture failed (%d); no verdict, nothing "
592:                  "retained\n", (int)frame_len);
593:           sc_enter(&state, SC_IDLE);
594:           return (int)frame_len;
595:         }
596: 
597:       printf("social_cue: captured %ld bytes, JPEG %dx%d\n",
598:              (long)frame_len, SC_WIDTH, SC_HEIGHT);
599:     }
600:   else
601:     {
602:       frame_len = 41984;
603:       printf("social_cue: mock frame, %ld bytes (camera not touched)\n",
604:              (long)frame_len);
605:     }
606: 
607:   if (g_cancelled)
608:     {
609:       sc_enter(&state, SC_CANCELLED);
610:       printf("social_cue: cancelled during capture; frame released, "
611:              "nothing reported\n");
612:       return OK;
613:     }
614: 
615:   sc_enter(&state, SC_ANALYZING);
616:   sc_print_request(frame_len);
617: 
618:   /* Where the HTTPS request goes.  Until then, a fixed response and a pause
619:    * long enough that the cancelled path is reachable by hand.
620:    */
621: 
622:   usleep(300 * 1000);
623: 
624:   if (g_cancelled)
625:     {
626:       sc_enter(&state, SC_CANCELLED);
627:       printf("social_cue: cancelled during analysis; result discarded\n");
628:       return OK;
629:     }
630: 
631:   sc_print_response(verdict);
632: 
633:   sc_enter(&state, SC_NOTIFYING);
634:   sc_notify(verdict);
635: 
636:   sc_enter(&state, SC_IDLE);
637:   printf("social_cue: frame released, no media or verdict retained\n");
638:   return OK;
639: }

13:  *   hello fb=0                 one panel only (default: every panel)

15:  * Only the newly written stroke is drawn each frame -- the pen adds ink, it

239:  *   Number of sizes collected for want_fmt, or a negated errno.

244:                             struct agent_camera_size_s *sizes,
245:                             size_t max_sizes, bool verbose)

249:   unsigned int i;

252:     {
253:       memset(&fmtdesc, 0, sizeof(fmtdesc));

255:       fmtdesc.type  = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;

351:  * Name: agent_camera_set_format
352:  *
353:  * Description:
354:  *   tool_camera.c's format step: ask for V4L2_PIX_FMT_JPEG and, if that is

356:  *
357:  *   When negotiate is true this also mirrors the geometry negotiation added
358:  *   to tool_camera.c by
359:  *   board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/ai_agent/0001-tool_camera-negotiate-frame-size.patch:
360:  *   a refused geometry is retried at the enumerated size whose pixel count
361:  *   is closest.  Same algorithm, same device, same driver, so `low` versus
362:  *   `low strict` is a direct before/after of that patch on this board.
363:  *
364:  *   Note that VIDIOC_ENUM_FRAMESIZES cannot be trusted to filter by pixel
365:  *   format: v4l2_cap.c's capture_enum_frmsize() indexes the imgsensor's

367:  *   enumerates every size.  VIDIOC_S_FMT is therefore the only authority on
368:  *   whether a (format, geometry) pair is real, which is why each candidate
369:  *   is put back through it rather than trusted because it was enumerated.

371:  ****************************************************************************/

373: static int agent_camera_set_format(int fd, int *width, int *height,
374:                                   bool negotiate, uint32_t *out_fmt)
375: {
376:   static const uint32_t candidates[] =
377:   {
378:     V4L2_PIX_FMT_JPEG,
379:     V4L2_PIX_FMT_ENTROPY,
380:   };
381: 
382:   struct agent_camera_size_s sizes[MAX_ENUM_SIZES];
383:   size_t c;
384: 
385:   for (c = 0; c < sizeof(candidates) / sizeof(candidates[0]); c++)
386:     {
387:       if (agent_camera_try_format(fd, *width, *height, candidates[c]) == OK)
388:         {
389:           *out_fmt = candidates[c];
390:           return OK;
391:         }
392: 
393:       printf("agent_camera: S_FMT ");
394:       agent_camera_print_fourcc(candidates[c]);
395:       printf(" %dx%d failed: %d\n", *width, *height, errno);
396:     }
397: 
398:   if (!negotiate)
399:     {
400:       return -EINVAL;
401:     }
402: 
403:   for (c = 0; c < sizeof(candidates) / sizeof(candidates[0]); c++)
404:     {
405:       unsigned long want = (unsigned long)(*width) *
406:                            (unsigned long)(*height);
407:       unsigned long best_delta = ULONG_MAX;
408:       int best_w = 0;
409:       int best_h = 0;
410:       int nsizes;
411:       int i;
412: 
413:       nsizes = agent_camera_enum(fd, candidates[c], sizes,
414:                                  MAX_ENUM_SIZES, false);
415:       if (nsizes <= 0)
416:         {
417:           continue;
418:         }
419: 
420:       for (i = 0; i < nsizes; i++)
421:         {
422:           unsigned long area = (unsigned long)sizes[i].width *
423:                                (unsigned long)sizes[i].height;
424:           unsigned long delta = area > want ? area - want : want - area;
425: 
426:           if (delta < best_delta)
427:             {
428:               best_delta = delta;
429:               best_w = sizes[i].width;
430:               best_h = sizes[i].height;
431:             }
432:         }
433: 
434:       if (best_w == 0 || (best_w == *width && best_h == *height))
435:         {
436:           continue;
437:         }
438: 
439:       if (agent_camera_try_format(fd, best_w, best_h, candidates[c]) == OK)
440:         {
441:           printf("agent_camera: %dx%d refused, using enumerated %dx%d\n",
442:                  *width, *height, best_w, best_h);
443:           *width   = best_w;
444:           *height  = best_h;
445:           *out_fmt = candidates[c];
446:           return OK;
447:         }
448:     }
449: 
450:   return -EINVAL;

453: /****************************************************************************
454:  * Name: agent_camera_check_jpeg
455:  *
456:  * Description:
457:  *   Reports whether the frame is a structurally valid JPEG file.
458:  *
459:  *   This used to check only SOI at the front and EOI at the end, and that
460:  *   judgement was wrong in a way worth spelling out: a frame can pass it and
461:  *   still be undecodable.  The encoder on this board emits
462:  *   SOI / APP0 / SOF0 / DQT / DHT and then entropy data with **no SOS
463:  *   segment**, so libjpeg rejects the file outright ("Invalid JPEG file

466:  *   -- see docs/reference/camera.md 14.6.

469:  *   encoder are preceded by 0xFF fill bytes (three of them, e.g.
470:  *   ff ff ff ff db); the standard permits that, and a scanner that does not
471:  *   skip fill will desynchronise and report segments that do not exist.
472:  *
473:  ****************************************************************************/
474: 
475: static void agent_camera_check_jpeg(const uint8_t *data, size_t len)
476: {
477:   bool have_sof = false;
478:   bool have_sos = false;
479:   bool have_dqt = false;
480:   bool have_dht = false;
481:   size_t i = 0;
482: 
483:   if (len < 4)
484:     {
485:       printf("agent_camera: frame too short to inspect (%zu bytes)\n", len);
486:       return;
487:     }
488: 
489:   if (data[0] != 0xff || data[1] != 0xd8)
490:     {
491:       printf("agent_camera: no SOI: starts %02x %02x\n", data[0], data[1]);
492:       return;
493:     }
494: 
495:   /* Walk the segments.  Stops at SOS, which is where entropy data begins. */
496: 
497:   i = 2;
498:   while (i + 1 < len)
499:     {
500:       uint8_t marker;
501:       size_t seglen;
502: 
503:       if (data[i] != 0xff)
504:         {
505:           break;
506:         }
507: 
508:       /* Skip fill bytes: any number of 0xFF may precede a marker. */
509: 
510:       while (i + 1 < len && data[i + 1] == 0xff)
511:         {
512:           i++;
513:         }
514: 
515:       if (i + 1 >= len)
516:         {
517:           break;
518:         }
519: 
520:       marker = data[i + 1];
521: 
522:       if (marker == 0xd9)
523:         {
524:           break;
525:         }
526: 
527:       if (marker == 0xda)
528:         {
529:           have_sos = true;
530:           break;
531:         }
532: 
533:       if (i + 3 >= len)
534:         {
535:           break;
536:         }
537: 
538:       seglen = ((size_t)data[i + 2] << 8) | data[i + 3];
539:       if (seglen < 2)
540:         {
541:           break;
542:         }
543: 
544:       switch (marker)
545:         {
546:           case 0xc0:
547:           case 0xc1:
548:             have_sof = true;
549:             break;
550: 
551:           case 0xdb:
552:             have_dqt = true;
553:             break;
554: 
555:           case 0xc4:
556:             have_dht = true;
557:             break;
558: 
559:           default:
560:             break;
561:         }
562: 
563:       i += 2 + seglen;
564:     }
565: 
566:   printf("agent_camera: structure SOF=%s DQT=%s DHT=%s SOS=%s EOI=%s\n",
567:          have_sof ? "yes" : "NO", have_dqt ? "yes" : "NO",
568:          have_dht ? "yes" : "NO", have_sos ? "yes" : "NO",
569:          (data[len - 2] == 0xff && data[len - 1] == 0xd9) ? "yes" : "NO");
570: 
571:   if (!have_sos)
572:     {
573:       printf("agent_camera: NOT a decodable JPEG -- no SOS segment, so the "
574:              "entropy data has no scan header.  A Vision LLM (or any "
575:              "standard decoder) will reject this.  See "
576:              "docs/reference/camera.md 14.6\n");
577:     }
578: }

580: /****************************************************************************
581:  * Name: agent_camera_print_b64
582:  *
583:  * Description:
584:  *   Prints the frame as base64 between two fence lines, so it can be pulled
585:  *   off the board without a filesystem.
586:  *
587:  *   The alternative is `hexdump` plus docs/tools/hexdump2raw.py, which works
588:  *   (and is what first got a frame onto the host) but needs a mounted
589:  *   filesystem, costs 4.4 bytes of console per payload byte -- a 35KB frame
590:  *   became 170KB of serial output -- and has to be parsed with tolerance for
591:  *   block headers, ANSI escapes and the ASCII column.  base64 is 1.37 bytes
592:  *   per byte and `base64 -d` is exact, so there is nothing to get wrong on
593:  *   the host side.
594:  *
595:  *   Written straight to stdout in 57-byte groups (76 base64 chars per line)
596:  *   with no intermediate buffer, because a second copy of a 160KB frame does
597:  *   not fit in the AP's kernel heap.
598:  *
599:  ****************************************************************************/
600: 
601: /****************************************************************************
602:  * Name: agent_camera_fnv1a
603:  *
604:  * Description:
605:  *   32-bit FNV-1a over the frame, printed next to the base64 fence so the
606:  *   host can prove the retrieval was lossless before drawing any conclusion
607:  *   about the picture.
608:  *
609:  *   This exists because two frames came back decoding only 8 rows while a
610:  *   third decoded fully, and "the board produced junk" and "the console
611:  *   dropped bytes" predict exactly the same thing on the host.  Length
612:  *   agreement does not separate them: a dropped chunk replaced by an
613:  *   interleaved driver log line keeps the byte count plausible.  FNV-1a is
614:  *   enough here (we are detecting loss, not defending against tampering)
615:  *   and costs one pass with no buffer.
616:  *
617:  ****************************************************************************/
618: 
619: static uint32_t agent_camera_fnv1a(const uint8_t *data, size_t len)
620: {
621:   uint32_t hash = 2166136261u;
622:   size_t i;
623: 
624:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
625:     {
626:       hash ^= (uint32_t)data[i];
627:       hash *= 16777619u;
628:     }
629: 
630:   return hash;
631: }
632: 
633: /****************************************************************************
634:  * Name: agent_camera_copy32
635:  *
636:  * Description:
637:  *   Word-at-a-time copy out of a capture buffer.  This libc's memcpy is
638:  *   byte-wise, and the source is non-cacheable PSRAM, so copying a ~28KB
639:  *   frame with it takes longer than the 33ms the sensor gives us between
640:  *   frames.  With only a couple of V4L2 buffers in flight that loses the
641:  *   race: the DMA reaches the buffer we are still reading and the frame
642:  *   comes out with a truncated scan -- SOI, EOI and every marker present, so
643:  *   the structure check passes, but a real decoder reports "broken data
644:  *   stream".  Measured before this existed: 3 of 29 recorded frames decoded.
645:  *
646:  *   Both ends are 4-byte aligned here (the capture buffers come from a PSRAM
647:  *   pool, the destination from malloc), and the tail is handled bytewise.
648:  *
649:  ****************************************************************************/
650: 
651: static void agent_camera_copy32(FAR uint8_t *dst, FAR const uint8_t *src,
652:                                 size_t len)
653: {
654:   FAR uint32_t *d = (FAR uint32_t *)dst;
655:   FAR const uint32_t *s = (FAR const uint32_t *)src;
656:   size_t words = len >> 2;
657:   size_t i;
658: 
659:   for (i = 0; i < words; i++)
660:     {
661:       d[i] = s[i];
662:     }
663: 
664:   for (i = words << 2; i < len; i++)
665:     {
666:       dst[i] = src[i];
667:     }
668: }
669: 
670: static void agent_camera_print_b64(const uint8_t *data, size_t len)
671: {
672:   static const char tbl[] =
673:     "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
674:   size_t i;
675: 
676:   printf("agent_camera: payload len=%zu fnv1a=0x%08" PRIx32 "\n",
677:          len, agent_camera_fnv1a(data, len));
678: 
679:   printf("-----BEGIN AGENT_CAMERA JPEG %zu-----\n", len);
680: 
681:   for (i = 0; i < len; i += 3)
682:     {
683:       size_t remain = len - i;
684:       uint32_t v = (uint32_t)data[i] << 16;
685:       char quad[4];
686: 
687:       if (remain > 1)
688:         {
689:           v |= (uint32_t)data[i + 1] << 8;
690:         }
691: 
692:       if (remain > 2)
693:         {
694:           v |= data[i + 2];
695:         }
696: 
697:       quad[0] = tbl[(v >> 18) & 0x3f];
698:       quad[1] = tbl[(v >> 12) & 0x3f];
699:       quad[2] = remain > 1 ? tbl[(v >> 6) & 0x3f] : '=';
700:       quad[3] = remain > 2 ? tbl[v & 0x3f] : '=';
701: 
702:       fwrite(quad, 1, 4, stdout);
703: 
704:       if ((i / 3) % 19 == 18)
705:         {
706:           fputc('\n', stdout);
707: 
708:           /* Throttle every 2 lines (~114 payload bytes, ~3.5KB/s).
709:            *
710:            * The console is the CP's UART0 with the AP's output arriving over
711:            * a mailbox bridge that holds 1024 bytes and flushes half-lines on
712:            * a 50ms timer.  A 30KB burst of base64 overruns it and the host
713:            * silently receives a truncated payload -- observed as 9111 of a
714:            * declared 22703 bytes, with a length that still looks plausible.
715:            * Pausing lets the bridge drain; the fnv1a line above is what
716:            * proves whether it worked.
717:            */
718: 
719:           if (((i / 3) / 19) % 2 == 1)
720:             {
721:               fflush(stdout);
722:               usleep(30000);
723:             }
724:         }
725:     }
726: 
727:   fputc('\n', stdout);
728:   printf("-----END AGENT_CAMERA JPEG-----\n");
729: }

762: /****************************************************************************
763:  * Name: agent_camera_teardown
764:  *
765:  * Description:
766:  *   Unwinds in tool_camera.c's order: STREAMOFF, munmap, REQBUFS(0),
767:  *   close.  REQBUFS(0) is what releases the PSRAM the imgdata allocator
768:  *   handed out; skipping it leaks a buffer heap that is larger than the
769:  *   whole AP kernel heap.
770:  *
771:  ****************************************************************************/
772: 
773: static void agent_camera_teardown(struct agent_camera_s *cam)
774: {
775:   enum v4l2_buf_type type = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
776:   struct v4l2_requestbuffers rel;
777:   uint32_t i;
778: 
779:   if (cam->fd < 0)
780:     {
781:       return;
782:     }
783: 
784:   if (cam->streaming)
785:     {
786:       ioctl(cam->fd, VIDIOC_STREAMOFF, (uintptr_t)&type);
787:       cam->streaming = false;
788:     }
789: 
790:   for (i = 0; i < cam->nbuffers; i++)
791:     {
792:       if (cam->bufs[i] != NULL && cam->bufs[i] != MAP_FAILED)
793:         {
794:           munmap(cam->bufs[i], cam->buflen[i]);
795:           cam->bufs[i] = NULL;
796:         }
797:     }
798: 
799:   memset(&rel, 0, sizeof(rel));
800:   rel.count  = 0;
801:   rel.type   = V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE;
802:   rel.memory = V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP;
803:   ioctl(cam->fd, VIDIOC_REQBUFS, (uintptr_t)&rel);
804: 
805:   close(cam->fd);
806:   cam->fd = -1;
807:   cam->nbuffers = 0;
808: }
